questions.question_text:
A supermarket wants to compare how many customers visited each of its branches: Harbour, Riverside, Central and Hilltop.
Which type of graph is most suitable?

options.why: A sector graph shows each branch as a share of the whole, rather than making the branch totals easy to compare.
The branches are unordered categories. Joining their totals suggests values between branch names that have no meaning.
Stem-and-leaf plots show the shape of a single numerical dataset, not a comparison of categories.

questions.solution_text:
The purpose is to compare the totals for separate categories (branches).
A column graph is most suitable.

questions.question_text:
A nurse records a patient’s temperature every hour and wants to show how it changes through the day.
Which type of graph is most suitable?

options.why: A column graph compares separate categories rather than showing continuous change over time.
A sector graph shows parts of a whole, not how a value changes across time.
A dot plot shows the shape of a dataset but does not track a value over time.

questions.solution_text:
Temperature over time is continuous data changing over time.
A line graph is most suitable.

questions.question_text:
A council wants one display showing what percentage of its waste is recycled, composted or sent to landfill, out of the total.
Which type of graph is most suitable?

options.why: A line graph shows change over time, not each category as a share of a total.
A dot plot shows the spread of numerical data, not percentages of a whole.
A stem-and-leaf plot displays numerical values, not parts of a whole.

questions.solution_text:
The purpose is to show parts of a whole as percentages.
A sector graph is most suitable.

questions.question_text:
A wildlife researcher records a flying bat’s height every minute and wants to show how its height changes during the flight.
Which type of graph is most suitable?

options.why: This treats the height readings as shares of a total, rather than showing how height changes during the flight.
This groups repeated heights and loses the time order needed to show the bat’s changing height.
This orders heights by place value rather than keeping each height paired with its recording time.

questions.solution_text:
Height is continuous numerical data recorded over time.
A line graph is most suitable because it keeps the readings in time order and shows how the bat’s height changes.

questions.solution_text:

A column graph should be used, because it compares the count for each plant type.

questions.question_text:
Students record how many times they use a vending machine in a week. The values are whole-number counts, and the purpose is to show the shape of their frequency distribution.
Which of these displays is most suitable?

options.why: A phonogram is not the appropriate standard display for this statistical data type.
A scattergraph represents paired bivariate data, not one discrete variable.
A sector graph shows shares of the whole rather than the shape of the distribution along a numerical axis.

questions.solution_text: A histogram shows the shape of a numerical frequency distribution. It can display discrete whole-number counts as well as continuous numerical data, so it is suitable here.

questions.question_text:
A sports shop records its total helmet sales for each month of a year. It wants to show how sales change across the year.
Which type of graph is most suitable?

options.why: A sector graph shows each month’s share of annual sales rather than the change in sales over time.
A stem-and-leaf plot groups the sales values by place value and loses their month-by-month order.
A histogram shows the frequency distribution of numerical sales values rather than which sales total belongs to each month.

questions.solution_text:
The purpose is to show changes in sales over time.
A line graph is most suitable because the months stay in time order and the line shows the trend across the year.
